about: The canonical cases for THE ONE OWNER RULE (who owns an account_ai_memory row) and the follow rule (which agents follow a rule, skill, shortcut or specialist), memory surfaces audit G9, 2026-09-29. Source of truth: hiveku_builder src/lib/olympus/memory-department.ts (resolveOwnerDepartment, resolveWriteOwnerDepartment, rowVisibleToAny, rowWritableByAny, foreignWriteIntent, followersOfOwner, rowFollowers, followedOnCalls; read its header) with parseIdentity in src/lib/olympus/agent-identity.ts (how front matter is read). The builder runs the module, the Memory page's browser copy (src/components/memory/sources/department-rows.ts) and the team summary's text-free path over these cases (src/lib/olympus/__tests__/memory-ownership-parity.test.ts); each Python agent server vendors this file byte for byte and runs its own copy of the rule (app/tools/memory_ownership.py) over it with pytest. Change the rule and this file together, then re-vendor. Every expectation was written by hand from the rule, never generated from the code.
rule: Typed rows are the domains that, trimmed and lower-cased, start with '_rule:', '_skill:', '_command:' or '_agent:'. '_account:_rule:x' is not one.
The column is the department column trimmed (JavaScript trim, which also strips U+FEFF and U+00A0) and lower-cased; empty is no column.

The marker is the FIRST '<!-- department: x -->' anywhere in the text: '<!--', whitespace, 'department:' (case-insensitive), whitespace, a word of [A-Za-z0-9_]+ (JavaScript's \w: compile Python patterns with re.ASCII), whitespace, '-->'. Its word is lower-cased. A later marker never counts.

Owner of a typed row: (a) the column when it is set and is not 'marketing', taken as written even when it names no department ('graphic_design', 'mini'); (b) when the column is empty or 'marketing' and the marker's word is in marketing_family, that topic; (c) column 'marketing' otherwise: 'marketing' (the Marketing parent); (d) no column: the marker when it names any canonical department, else the front matter's department when it names one, else the shape of the domain (none for a typed row): no owner (null, shared with every agent).

(b) is the only change from the column-first rule: it moves a row only between 'marketing' and one of its topics. The front matter never beats a 'marketing' column, and neither does a marker naming a department outside the family.

Every other row is decided as before: 'account' and 'account-suggestions' (trimmed, any case) are owned by 'account'; an '_identity:x' row by its slug when x is a canonical department, else by its front matter's department (not checked against the list), and never by a marker or its column (the write owner falls back to the column); anything else by the column, else the marker or front matter naming a canonical department, else the domain's own name when that is a department.

Front matter: skip ONE leading marker line (ASCII whitespace around it, [A-Za-z0-9_]+ word, then LF), then the text must open with '---\n'. A byte-order mark, a CR LF or anything else before it declares nothing (as in identity-pick-cases.json). A 'department:' line elsewhere in the prose is not a declaration.

canonical departments: marketing_family plus sales, helpdesk, production, accounting, comms, coder, orchestrator (follower_departments). 'analytics' is a Marketing topic; 'graphic_design' is no department.

departments / visible / writable / foreign: rowVisibleToAny(row, departments) is true when the owner is null, false when it is 'account', else whether the owner is in departments (trimmed, lower-cased). rowWritableByAny is the same over write_owner. foreign is foreignWriteIntent(row.domain, row.content, departments): the first department the caller's domain and text could land the row in that departments do not cover, or null ('account' for account memory; for an identity its slug, else its front matter; else the domain shape and the in-text declaration (marker, else front matter, canonical only), both).
follow_rule: followers is null for a row that is not a rule, skill, shortcut or specialist: a profile follows the profile rule (identity-pick-cases.json), a note is its owner's own, '_account:*' rows are placed by their name, About your business is read through its own loader.
A website's own row (project_id set): ['coder'], the website agent on that website only, whoever owns it.

No owner (shared with every agent): every agent in follower_departments, the chief of staff included (Abe's decision 5; her server still leaves out a rule that briefs her on a department that is switched off, a matter of the account's switches, not of the row).

An owner in follower_departments: that agent. 'marketing' is ALSO followed by every Marketing topic. The website agent ('coder') also follows website_agent_followed_owners, and website_agent_followed_skill_owners for a skill only (SEO's skills, never its rules).
'orchestrator': nobody. The chief of staff's rules and skills are her '_account:*' rows; a typed row filed for her outside them is one she never reads (the Memory page hides it).
An owner that names no agent ('account', 'graphic_design', 'mini'): nobody.

on_calls (followedOnCalls): a phone call carries only the receptionist's own call rules: an account-level '_rule:' row owned by 'comms' whose text has no '<!-- origin: reflection -->' marker (the communications server's kept_on_public_call). Never a shared rule, a skill, a shortcut or a specialist (Abe's decision 2).
Compare followers as sets; they are sorted here.
row_fields: domain, department (the column as stored, or null), project_id (null for an account-level row), content.
expect_fields: owner = resolveOwnerDepartment(row); write_owner = resolveWriteOwnerDepartment(row); visible = rowVisibleToAny(row, departments); writable = rowWritableByAny(row, departments); foreign = foreignWriteIntent(row.domain, row.content, departments); followers = rowFollowers(row); on_calls = followedOnCalls(row).
